Creating Records ​

postRecord(_:config:files:) creates a record, or updates one when the config has a record_id. It returns the saved record (see The record).

swift
import Skapi

let skapi = try Skapi(projectId: "<Project ID>")

let record = try await skapi.postRecord(
    ["title": "Hello", "body": "My first post"],                     // data
    config: ["table": ["name": "posts", "access_group": "public"]]   // config
)
print(record["record_id"]?.string ?? "", record["data"]?["title"]?.string ?? "")

data ​

data is any JSON value: an object, an array, a string, a number, a boolean, or .null.

  • Left out (or nil), the stored data is kept. This only matters on an update: skapi.postRecord(config: [...]).
  • .null stores null.
  • Up to 2 MB as JSON. More throws INVALID_REQUEST: Data should not exceed 2MB.

Data larger than 32 KB is kept in file storage instead of the database. You do not have to do anything about it: reading the record gives back the value you posted.

Your own Codable types go in with try JSON(encoding: value), see Codable types.

config ​

keytype
tableobject["name", "access_group"]. Required when creating. A left-out access_group means "public" when creating (signed-out callers must write it), and keeps the record's group when updating. See access groups.
record_idstringUpdate this record instead of creating one. A unique ID works too.
unique_idstring or .nullYour own ID for the record, unique in the project. .null removes it on an update. See Unique IDs.
readonlybooltrue makes the record unchangeable.
indexobject or .null["name", "value"], one searchable value: a string, number or bool. .null removes it. See Indexes.
tagsarray of strings, or a comma-separated stringLabels to search by. [] removes them on an update. See Tags.
referencestring, object or .nullThe record ID or unique ID of a record this one refers to. .null removes it. See References.
sourceobjectRules for records that reference this one. See Reference rules.
remove_binarray or .nullUpdates only: files to take off the record. See Files.

files: attaches files. See Files.

Read-only records ​

swift
let rec = try await skapi.postRecord(
    ["order": 1042, "total": 59.0],
    config: ["table": ["name": "orders", "access_group": "private"], "readonly": true]
)

A read-only record cannot be updated or deleted by its uploader. An update throws INVALID_REQUEST: Record is read only.

Tags, index and unique ID ​

swift
try await skapi.postRecord(
    ["title": "Getz/Gilberto", "artist": "Stan Getz, Joao Gilberto"],
    config: [
        "table": ["name": "albums", "access_group": "public"],
        "unique_id": "album:getz-gilberto",
        "index": ["name": "year", "value": 1964],
        "tags": ["jazz", "bossa nova"],
    ]
)

Each record has at most one index and any number of tags. How to query them is in Indexes, Tags and Unique IDs.

Reference and source ​

swift
let post = try await skapi.postRecord(
    ["text": "What do you think?"],
    config: ["table": ["name": "posts", "access_group": "public"],
             "source": ["prevent_multiple_referencing": true]]
)

try await skapi.postRecord(
    ["text": "I like it"],
    config: ["table": ["name": "comments", "access_group": "public"],
             "reference": post["record_id"] ?? .null]
)

See References.

Many records at once ​

postRecords(_😃 takes an array of ["data", "config"] items and saves them 100 to a request. A thousand rows are ten requests instead of a thousand.

swift
let items: [JSON] = rows.map { row in
    ["data": row, "config": ["table": ["name": "imports", "access_group": "public"]]]
}
let result = try await skapi.postRecords(items)

print(result["list"]?.array?.count ?? 0, "saved")
for f in result["failed"]?.array ?? [] {
    print(f["index"]?.int ?? -1, f["code"]?.string ?? "", f["message"]?.string ?? "")
}
json
{
  "list": [record, ...],
  "failed": [
    {"index": 7, "code": "INVALID_PARAMETER", "message": "..."}
  ]
}

list holds the saved records in the order given, and failed the items that were not saved, by position. Each item follows the rules of postRecord, with the same config keys. A refused item does not stop the others, and the counts of list and failed add up to the number of items. Only a failed request (network, sign-in, a server error) throws; records saved by earlier requests stay saved. postRecords does not attach files: use uploadFiles on the saved records.
